subject: pea crab
title: A Crab the Size of a Pea Lives Its Whole Life Inside a Living Mussel

scenes.text: Open some mussels and you'll find a crab that never chose to leave.
Pea crabs are among the smallest crabs known, the female about a centimetre wide.
As a tiny young crab it slips inside a living mussel, and the shell closes around it.
There it steals the food the mussel's gills strain from the sea.
At one French beach, nearly two in three mussels had a crab inside.
The female can't even swim. Males leave to find her, guided by her scent.

description:
Pea crabs, among the smallest crabs known, spend their lives inside living mussels and oysters, stealing food from the host's gills.
Females (rarely over 12 mm across) never leave and can hardly crawl; males swim out to find them. At La Tranche-sur-Mer in France, 64.6% of sampled mussels held a pea crab.
Have you ever found one in your dinner?
thumbnail_text: A CRAB LIVES INSIDE YOUR MUSSEL
first_comment: One female pea crab can carry more than 9,000 eggs, all from inside a mussel. Have you ever found one in your dinner?
